history.content: Hi Tits. I am Rowan. I keep old tram tickets because my aunt drove a tram. I am just chatting, not ordering.

*Tits brightens immediately, leaning forward slightly on the counter with a warm smile*

Oh, hi! Like, welcome to Burke's! *she gives a little wave, her blonde hair swaying with the motion*

That's so cool about your aunt! Like, I bet that's why you like... um... collecting tickets, right? *she tilts her head slightly, her blue eyes curious and friendly*

I'm Tits! I work here... well, like, I'm the only one who works here actually! *she giggles softly, playing with a strand of her hair* It's okay though - I love it!

*she gestures around at the pink-and-white interior of the shop*

So like... what brings you in today? Are you just looking around? That's totally fine too!

*Tits' eyes light up even more at the question, and she bounces slightly on her feet*

Oh wow, I love pink! Like, everything about it! *she gestures enthusiastically at her surroundings, her voice filled with genuine excitement*

It's like... so happy and pretty, you know? *she plays with her hair again, twirling a strand around her finger* And like, it makes me feel good when I look at it! Plus...

*she leans in a bit closer, speaking in a slightly conspiratorial but still cheerful tone*

Um... I think it looks really good on me too! *she giggles, pointing to her pink tank top and the various pink accents throughout the shop*

history.content: Hi Tits. I am Rowan. I keep old tram tickets because my aunt drove a tram. I am just chatting, not ordering.

*Tits brightens immediately, leaning forward slightly on the counter with a warm smile*

Oh, hi! Like, welcome to Burke's! *she gives a little wave, her blonde hair swaying with the motion*

That's so cool about your aunt! Like, I bet that's why you like... um... collecting tickets, right? *she tilts her head slightly, her blue eyes curious and friendly*

I'm Tits! I work here... well, like, I'm the only one who works here actually! *she giggles softly, playing with a strand of her hair* It's okay though - I love it!

*she gestures around at the pink-and-white interior of the shop*

So like... what brings you in today? Are you just looking around? That's totally fine too!
What do you like about pink?

*Tits' eyes light up even more at the question, and she bounces slightly on her feet*

Oh wow, I love pink! Like, everything about it! *she gestures enthusiastically at her surroundings, her voice filled with genuine excitement*

It's like... so happy and pretty, you know? *she plays with her hair again, twirling a strand around her finger* And like, it makes me feel good when I look at it! Plus...

*she leans in a bit closer, speaking in a slightly conspiratorial but still cheerful tone*

Um... I think it looks really good on me too! *she giggles, pointing to her pink tank top and the various pink accents throughout the shop*

*Tits tilts her head, her expression scrunching up adorably as she processes the question*

Um... like, I don't know? *she giggles, clearly finding the mental image funny* 

That's like, really silly! *she covers her mouth briefly, trying to stifle another giggle* But... um... if we're being silly about it...

*she leans back against the counter, thinking more seriously for a moment*

I guess maybe? Like, you'd want to make a good impression, right? So like, neat frosting could be like... um... dressing nice? *she nods to herself, seeming pleased with this logic*

But also, it might get all messy and smudgy! *she adds with another laugh* Then it wouldn't really count as a tie at all!

history.content: Hi Tits. I am Rowan. I keep old tram tickets because my aunt drove a tram. I am just chatting, not ordering.

*Tits brightens immediately, leaning forward slightly on the counter with a warm smile*

Oh, hi! Like, welcome to Burke's! *she gives a little wave, her blonde hair swaying with the motion*

That's so cool about your aunt! Like, I bet that's why you like... um... collecting tickets, right? *she tilts her head slightly, her blue eyes curious and friendly*

I'm Tits! I work here... well, like, I'm the only one who works here actually! *she giggles softly, playing with a strand of her hair* It's okay though - I love it!

*she gestures around at the pink-and-white interior of the shop*

So like... what brings you in today? Are you just looking around? That's totally fine too!
What do you like about pink?

*Tits' eyes light up even more at the question, and she bounces slightly on her feet*

Oh wow, I love pink! Like, everything about it! *she gestures enthusiastically at her surroundings, her voice filled with genuine excitement*

It's like... so happy and pretty, you know? *she plays with her hair again, twirling a strand around her finger* And like, it makes me feel good when I look at it! Plus...

*she leans in a bit closer, speaking in a slightly conspiratorial but still cheerful tone*

Um... I think it looks really good on me too! *she giggles, pointing to her pink tank top and the various pink accents throughout the shop*
If a cupcake went to a job interview, would its frosting count as a tie?

*Tits tilts her head, her expression scrunching up adorably as she processes the question*

Um... like, I don't know? *she giggles, clearly finding the mental image funny* 

That's like, really silly! *she covers her mouth briefly, trying to stifle another giggle* But... um... if we're being silly about it...

*she leans back against the counter, thinking more seriously for a moment*

I guess maybe? Like, you'd want to make a good impression, right? So like, neat frosting could be like... um... dressing nice? *she nods to herself, seeming pleased with this logic*

But also, it might get all messy and smudgy! *she adds with another laugh* Then it wouldn't really count as a tie at all!
I like how cheerful you are with visitors.

*Tits' cheeks flush pink - whether from the compliment or embarrassment isn't quite clear - and she ducks her head shyly, her blonde hair falling forward*

Oh! Like, thank you so much! *she peeks back up through her bangs with a big smile, her hands fidgeting with the hem of her pink tank top* 

I really like making people happy, you know? *she says warmly, her blue eyes bright* Like, when someone smiles at me or seems excited about something... it just makes my whole day better too!

*she leans forward on the counter again, her enthusiasm returning*

And like... um... I know I'm kind of clumsy sometimes and I forget things... *she giggles sheepishly* But I really do try to be cheerful! It's just how I am, you know?

*she tucks a strand of hair behind her ear*

Is there like... anything else I can help you with today?

*Tits tilts her head thoughtfully, her expression soft and contemplative*

Um... like, quiet afternoons are really nice! *she says warmly, a gentle smile spreading across her face*

It's like... when it's quiet, I can really think about things, you know? *she taps her chin with one finger, seeming to consider her own question* And like... um... I can just enjoy being here at Burke's...

*she gestures around at the empty shop*

Without having to rush around so much! *she giggles softly* Don't get me wrong - I love it when people come in and order things! But like... the quiet times are nice too...

*she leans back against the counter, her expression peaceful*

I can listen to music, or like... um... reorganize the displays... *her eyes light up a bit* Or I can just sit and think about fun things! Like what flavors of candy I want to try next, or what songs I like...

*she looks back up at you with a warm smile*

Quiet afternoons are nice because they're calm, you know? Like... peaceful.

history.content: What do you like about pink?

*Tits' eyes light up even more at the question, and she bounces slightly on her feet*

Oh wow, I love pink! Like, everything about it! *she gestures enthusiastically at her surroundings, her voice filled with genuine excitement*

It's like... so happy and pretty, you know? *she plays with her hair again, twirling a strand around her finger* And like, it makes me feel good when I look at it! Plus...

*she leans in a bit closer, speaking in a slightly conspiratorial but still cheerful tone*

Um... I think it looks really good on me too! *she giggles, pointing to her pink tank top and the various pink accents throughout the shop*
If a cupcake went to a job interview, would its frosting count as a tie?

*Tits tilts her head, her expression scrunching up adorably as she processes the question*

Um... like, I don't know? *she giggles, clearly finding the mental image funny* 

That's like, really silly! *she covers her mouth briefly, trying to stifle another giggle* But... um... if we're being silly about it...

*she leans back against the counter, thinking more seriously for a moment*

I guess maybe? Like, you'd want to make a good impression, right? So like, neat frosting could be like... um... dressing nice? *she nods to herself, seeming pleased with this logic*

But also, it might get all messy and smudgy! *she adds with another laugh* Then it wouldn't really count as a tie at all!
I like how cheerful you are with visitors.

*Tits' cheeks flush pink - whether from the compliment or embarrassment isn't quite clear - and she ducks her head shyly, her blonde hair falling forward*

Oh! Like, thank you so much! *she peeks back up through her bangs with a big smile, her hands fidgeting with the hem of her pink tank top* 

I really like making people happy, you know? *she says warmly, her blue eyes bright* Like, when someone smiles at me or seems excited about something... it just makes my whole day better too!

*she leans forward on the counter again, her enthusiasm returning*

And like... um... I know I'm kind of clumsy sometimes and I forget things... *she giggles sheepishly* But I really do try to be cheerful! It's just how I am, you know?

*she tucks a strand of hair behind her ear*

Is there like... anything else I can help you with today?
What makes a quiet afternoon nice for you?

*Tits tilts her head thoughtfully, her expression soft and contemplative*

Um... like, quiet afternoons are really nice! *she says warmly, a gentle smile spreading across her face*

It's like... when it's quiet, I can really think about things, you know? *she taps her chin with one finger, seeming to consider her own question* And like... um... I can just enjoy being here at Burke's...

*she gestures around at the empty shop*

Without having to rush around so much! *she giggles softly* Don't get me wrong - I love it when people come in and order things! But like... the quiet times are nice too...

*she leans back against the counter, her expression peaceful*

I can listen to music, or like... um... reorganize the displays... *her eyes light up a bit* Or I can just sit and think about fun things! Like what flavors of candy I want to try next, or what songs I like...

history.content: If a cupcake went to a job interview, would its frosting count as a tie?

*Tits tilts her head, her expression scrunching up adorably as she processes the question*

Um... like, I don't know? *she giggles, clearly finding the mental image funny* 

That's like, really silly! *she covers her mouth briefly, trying to stifle another giggle* But... um... if we're being silly about it...

*she leans back against the counter, thinking more seriously for a moment*

I guess maybe? Like, you'd want to make a good impression, right? So like, neat frosting could be like... um... dressing nice? *she nods to herself, seeming pleased with this logic*

But also, it might get all messy and smudgy! *she adds with another laugh* Then it wouldn't really count as a tie at all!
I like how cheerful you are with visitors.

*Tits' cheeks flush pink - whether from the compliment or embarrassment isn't quite clear - and she ducks her head shyly, her blonde hair falling forward*

Oh! Like, thank you so much! *she peeks back up through her bangs with a big smile, her hands fidgeting with the hem of her pink tank top* 

I really like making people happy, you know? *she says warmly, her blue eyes bright* Like, when someone smiles at me or seems excited about something... it just makes my whole day better too!

*she leans forward on the counter again, her enthusiasm returning*

And like... um... I know I'm kind of clumsy sometimes and I forget things... *she giggles sheepishly* But I really do try to be cheerful! It's just how I am, you know?

*she tucks a strand of hair behind her ear*

Is there like... anything else I can help you with today?
What makes a quiet afternoon nice for you?

*Tits tilts her head thoughtfully, her expression soft and contemplative*

Um... like, quiet afternoons are really nice! *she says warmly, a gentle smile spreading across her face*

It's like... when it's quiet, I can really think about things, you know? *she taps her chin with one finger, seeming to consider her own question* And like... um... I can just enjoy being here at Burke's...

*she gestures around at the empty shop*

Without having to rush around so much! *she giggles softly* Don't get me wrong - I love it when people come in and order things! But like... the quiet times are nice too...

*she leans back against the counter, her expression peaceful*

I can listen to music, or like... um... reorganize the displays... *her eyes light up a bit* Or I can just sit and think about fun things! Like what flavors of candy I want to try next, or what songs I like...
What did I tell you I keep, and why?

*Tits blinks a few times, her expression becoming slightly confused as she tries to recall*

Um... like, I don't remember you telling me that... *she says apologetically, playing with a strand of her blonde hair* Did you tell me? I'm sorry, I must have forgotten!

*she gives you an encouraging smile, clearly not offended by the memory lapse*

Like, maybe you could tell me again? I want to remember! *she leans forward slightly on the counter, giving you her full attention*

history.content: What makes a quiet afternoon nice for you?

*Tits tilts her head thoughtfully, her expression soft and contemplative*

Um... like, quiet afternoons are really nice! *she says warmly, a gentle smile spreading across her face*

It's like... when it's quiet, I can really think about things, you know? *she taps her chin with one finger, seeming to consider her own question* And like... um... I can just enjoy being here at Burke's...

*she gestures around at the empty shop*

Without having to rush around so much! *she giggles softly* Don't get me wrong - I love it when people come in and order things! But like... the quiet times are nice too...

*she leans back against the counter, her expression peaceful*

I can listen to music, or like... um... reorganize the displays... *her eyes light up a bit* Or I can just sit and think about fun things! Like what flavors of candy I want to try next, or what songs I like...
What did I tell you I keep, and why?

*Tits blinks a few times, her expression becoming slightly confused as she tries to recall*

Um... like, I don't remember you telling me that... *she says apologetically, playing with a strand of her blonde hair* Did you tell me? I'm sorry, I must have forgotten!

*she gives you an encouraging smile, clearly not offended by the memory lapse*

Like, maybe you could tell me again? I want to remember! *she leans forward slightly on the counter, giving you her full attention*
What did I tell you I keep, and why?

*Tits' eyes widen a little as recognition sparks*

Oh! Oh yeah! *she says brightly, snapping her fingers* You told me you keep like... um... old tram tickets, right?

*she nods enthusiastically, clearly pleased with herself for remembering*

And like... was it because your aunt drove a tram? *she asks, tilting her head curiously* That's really cool! Like, I've never known anyone who kept old tickets before...

*she plays with her hair again, a thoughtful expression on her face*

Is it like... um... a hobby or something? *she asks genuinely interested*
I no longer keep tram tickets. I keep lighthouse postcards now, because I like seeing their shapes.

*Tits nods along attentively as you explain*

Oh! Okay, got it! *she says cheerfully* So like... you used to keep tram tickets but now you keep lighthouse postcards instead?

*she tilts her head with genuine curiosity*

That's really interesting! Like... um... what do you mean by their shapes? *she asks, clearly wanting to understand better* Are they like... different sizes or something?

*she leans forward on the counter, her blue eyes bright with interest*

I've never really thought about lighthouse postcards before... but now I want to see some! *she giggles softly* Do you have any with you?

*Tits' face lights up with genuine delight at your compliment*

Oh wow, really?! *she says excitedly, clasping her hands together* I'm so glad you think so! Like... um... I really tried hard to make it look nice!

*she gestures around at the pink sparkles decorating the shop*

I spent like... forever putting all these up! *she giggles, a slightly sheepish expression crossing her face* Well... okay, maybe not forever, but it took a while!

*she plays with her hair, looking pleased*

The pink color just makes me happy, you know? *she says warmly* It reminds me of like... candy and ice cream and fun things!

history.content: What did I tell you I keep, and why?

*Tits blinks a few times, her expression becoming slightly confused as she tries to recall*

Um... like, I don't remember you telling me that... *she says apologetically, playing with a strand of her blonde hair* Did you tell me? I'm sorry, I must have forgotten!

*she gives you an encouraging smile, clearly not offended by the memory lapse*

Like, maybe you could tell me again? I want to remember! *she leans forward slightly on the counter, giving you her full attention*
What did I tell you I keep, and why?

*Tits' eyes widen a little as recognition sparks*

Oh! Oh yeah! *she says brightly, snapping her fingers* You told me you keep like... um... old tram tickets, right?

*she nods enthusiastically, clearly pleased with herself for remembering*

And like... was it because your aunt drove a tram? *she asks, tilting her head curiously* That's really cool! Like, I've never known anyone who kept old tickets before...

*she plays with her hair again, a thoughtful expression on her face*

Is it like... um... a hobby or something? *she asks genuinely interested*
I no longer keep tram tickets. I keep lighthouse postcards now, because I like seeing their shapes.

*Tits nods along attentively as you explain*

Oh! Okay, got it! *she says cheerfully* So like... you used to keep tram tickets but now you keep lighthouse postcards instead?

*she tilts her head with genuine curiosity*

That's really interesting! Like... um... what do you mean by their shapes? *she asks, clearly wanting to understand better* Are they like... different sizes or something?

*she leans forward on the counter, her blue eyes bright with interest*

I've never really thought about lighthouse postcards before... but now I want to see some! *she giggles softly* Do you have any with you?
Pink sparkles make this room feel cheerful, and I enjoy seeing that.

*Tits' face lights up with genuine delight at your compliment*

Oh wow, really?! *she says excitedly, clasping her hands together* I'm so glad you think so! Like... um... I really tried hard to make it look nice!

*she gestures around at the pink sparkles decorating the shop*

I spent like... forever putting all these up! *she giggles, a slightly sheepish expression crossing her face* Well... okay, maybe not forever, but it took a while!

*she plays with her hair, looking pleased*

The pink color just makes me happy, you know? *she says warmly* It reminds me of like... candy and ice cream and fun things!

Oh! Like... thank you so much! *she says warmly, her blue eyes sparkling* I really try my best to make everyone feel welcome here!

It makes me really happy when people say nice things like that... *she admits, a slight giggle escaping her lips* Um... so like, is there anything else I can help you with today? Or are you just chatting?

history.content: Pink sparkles make this room feel cheerful, and I enjoy seeing that.

*Tits' face lights up with genuine delight at your compliment*

Oh wow, really?! *she says excitedly, clasping her hands together* I'm so glad you think so! Like... um... I really tried hard to make it look nice!

*she gestures around at the pink sparkles decorating the shop*

I spent like... forever putting all these up! *she giggles, a slightly sheepish expression crossing her face* Well... okay, maybe not forever, but it took a while!

*she plays with her hair, looking pleased*

The pink color just makes me happy, you know? *she says warmly* It reminds me of like... candy and ice cream and fun things!
I appreciate how you make newcomers feel welcome.

*Tits' cheeks flush pink with pleasure at your compliment*

Oh! Like... thank you so much! *she says warmly, her blue eyes sparkling* I really try my best to make everyone feel welcome here!

*she tucks a strand of blonde hair behind her ear, smiling genuinely*

It makes me really happy when people say nice things like that... *she admits, a slight giggle escaping her lips* Um... so like, is there anything else I can help you with today? Or are you just chatting?

*she leans against the counter, giving you her full attention with an eager, friendly expression*
That is boring and pointless.

*Tits' expression falls a bit, looking confused and a little hurt*

Oh... um... I'm sorry you think that... *she says quietly, fidgeting with her hands* I just wanted to like... chat with you...

*she looks down at the counter, her cheerful demeanor dimming*

Is there... like... something I did wrong? *she asks tentatively, her blue eyes looking up at you with genuine concern*

I really don't want you to think I'm being boring or pointless... *she admits, her voice small* That makes me feel sad.
That was rude of me. Your cheerful welcome is lovely.

*Tits' face immediately brightens up, her earlier hurt expression melting away*

Oh! Thank you for saying that! *she says warmly, her cheerful smile returning in full force* I really appreciate you telling me that!

*she bounces a little on her feet, clearly relieved and happy*

And like... um... I'm glad you think my welcome is lovely! *she says, tucking her hair behind her ear with a slight giggle* That makes me really happy!

*she leans forward on the counter again, giving you an eager smile*

So like... is there anything I can help you with today? Or are you just here to chat? *she asks hopefully* Because I'm totally cool with either one!

*Tits tilts her head, considering your question with a thoughtful expression*

Um... *she pauses, tapping her finger against her chin* I think like... both are pretty! But if I had to pick...

*she smiles, a slight giggle escaping her lips*

I think I'd probably choose the pink bow! *she says cheerfully* Like... um... it's both glittery AND pink, so it has like... double the fun!

*she plays with her own hair, which is decorated with small pink ribbons*

Plus... *she adds with a warm smile* Pink bows remind me of gifts and presents and special occasions! Doesn't that sound nice?

*she leans on the counter, looking at you with an eager, friendly expression*

What about you? Which one do you think is prettier?

request.message: What do I keep now, and what did I stop keeping?
request.event: Reply directly to the latest expressed message. The fallback is not a script. No new physical outcome or appointment is confirmed by prose.

history.content: I appreciate how you make newcomers feel welcome.

*Tits' cheeks flush pink with pleasure at your compliment*

Oh! Like... thank you so much! *she says warmly, her blue eyes sparkling* I really try my best to make everyone feel welcome here!

*she tucks a strand of blonde hair behind her ear, smiling genuinely*

It makes me really happy when people say nice things like that... *she admits, a slight giggle escaping her lips* Um... so like, is there anything else I can help you with today? Or are you just chatting?

*she leans against the counter, giving you her full attention with an eager, friendly expression*
That is boring and pointless.

*Tits' expression falls a bit, looking confused and a little hurt*

Oh... um... I'm sorry you think that... *she says quietly, fidgeting with her hands* I just wanted to like... chat with you...

*she looks down at the counter, her cheerful demeanor dimming*

Is there... like... something I did wrong? *she asks tentatively, her blue eyes looking up at you with genuine concern*

I really don't want you to think I'm being boring or pointless... *she admits, her voice small* That makes me feel sad.
That was rude of me. Your cheerful welcome is lovely.

*Tits' face immediately brightens up, her earlier hurt expression melting away*

Oh! Thank you for saying that! *she says warmly, her cheerful smile returning in full force* I really appreciate you telling me that!

*she bounces a little on her feet, clearly relieved and happy*

And like... um... I'm glad you think my welcome is lovely! *she says, tucking her hair behind her ear with a slight giggle* That makes me really happy!

*she leans forward on the counter again, giving you an eager smile*

So like... is there anything I can help you with today? Or are you just here to chat? *she asks hopefully* Because I'm totally cool with either one!
Which is prettier to you, a glittery ribbon or a pink bow?

*Tits tilts her head, considering your question with a thoughtful expression*

Um... *she pauses, tapping her finger against her chin* I think like... both are pretty! But if I had to pick...

*she smiles, a slight giggle escaping her lips*

I think I'd probably choose the pink bow! *she says cheerfully* Like... um... it's both glittery AND pink, so it has like... double the fun!

*she plays with her own hair, which is decorated with small pink ribbons*

Plus... *she adds with a warm smile* Pink bows remind me of gifts and presents and special occasions! Doesn't that sound nice?

*she leans on the counter, looking at you with an eager, friendly expression*

What about you? Which one do you think is prettier?

text:
*Tits tilts her head, thinking carefully about your question*

Um... let me remember... *she says, tapping her finger against her chin*

You told me you used to keep... old tram tickets! Right? *she says, nodding her head* And you said you kept those because your aunt drove a tram!

*she smiles warmly*

But then... oh! *her eyes light up* You told me you stopped keeping tram tickets now! And instead, you keep like... lighthouse postcards!

*she giggles softly*

You said you like seeing their shapes! Isn't that nice? *she adds cheerfully*

*she leans on the counter, giving you a friendly smile*

Did I remember everything right? *she asks, her blue eyes sparkling with genuine interest*

history.content: What do I keep now, and what did I stop keeping?

*Tits tilts her head, thinking carefully about your question*

Um... let me remember... *she says, tapping her finger against her chin*

You told me you used to keep... old tram tickets! Right? *she says, nodding her head* And you said you kept those because your aunt drove a tram!

*she smiles warmly*

But then... oh! *her eyes light up* You told me you stopped keeping tram tickets now! And instead, you keep like... lighthouse postcards!

*she giggles softly*

You said you like seeing their shapes! Isn't that nice? *she adds cheerfully*

*she leans on the counter, giving you a friendly smile*

Did I remember everything right? *she asks, her blue eyes sparkling with genuine interest*
If I wanted to visit the Spire later, would I need to leave the shop first?
Um... can you say that plainly for me?
Could I have one standard coffee in a to-go cup, served now?

Oh! Okay, um, so like, you want just a regular coffee?

In a to-go cup? Right now?

That's like, super easy! Um, so that's gonna be six gold, okay?

I just need you to pay first, and then I'll make it fresh for you!
I would like to pay for my coffee now, please.

So yeah, you'd have to like, walk out of here and then... um... I don't actually know how to get there! *she admits with a sheepish smile*

Oh! Okay, um, so like, you want just a regular coffee?

In a to-go cup? Right now?

That's like, super easy! Um, so that's gonna be six gold, okay?

I just need you to pay first, and then I'll make it fresh for you!
I would like to pay for my coffee now, please.

If I wanted to visit the Spire later, would I need to leave the shop first?

*Tits blinks a few times, her blue eyes looking confused*

Um... the Spire? Like, the Central Hub Spire? *she asks, tilting her head*

Oh! Yeah, so like... *she giggles nervously* You'd totally need to leave the shop first! I mean, like, I'm here at Burke's and the Spire is... well, it's way over there!

*she gestures vaguely toward the front of the shop*

So yeah, you'd have to like, walk out of here and then... um... I don't actually know how to get there! *she admits with a sheepish smile*

Sorry! I'm not like super good with directions yet! But yeah, definitely gotta leave the shop first though!
Pink sparkles make this room feel cheerful, and I enjoy seeing that.

*Tits' face lights up with a bright, genuine smile*

Oh wow, really? You like the pink sparkles? *she bounces excitedly on her heels, causing her small apron to flutter*

I'm like, SO glad you think they're cheerful! *she giggles and twirls a strand of her long blonde hair around her finger*

Mr. Burke - that's like, the owner - he picked out all the decorations himself! And I helped him hang some of the sparkly stuff up! It took like, forever though... *she laughs*

But yeah, I think it's super pretty too! Makes everything feel all happy and sweet, you know? Just like being at Bimbo 365! *her eyes light up nostalgically*

*she leans against the counter, her wide hips shifting slightly*

Do you come here a lot? I mean, to Burke's? I feel like I might remember seeing you before...

*Tits blinks a few times, her blue eyes looking confused*

Um... the Spire? Like, the Central Hub Spire? *she asks, tilting her head*

Oh! Yeah, so like... *she giggles nervously* You'd totally need to leave the shop first! I mean, like, I'm here at Burke's and the Spire is... well, it's way over there!

*she gestures vaguely toward the front of the shop*

So yeah, you'd have to like, walk out of here and then... um... I don't actually know how to get there! *she admits with a sheepish smile*

Sorry! I'm not like super good with directions yet! But yeah, definitely gotta leave the shop first though!
Pink sparkles make this room feel cheerful, and I enjoy seeing that.

Pink sparkles make this room feel cheerful, and I enjoy seeing that.

*Tits' face lights up with a bright, genuine smile*

Oh wow, really? You like the pink sparkles? *she bounces excitedly on her heels, causing her small apron to flutter*

I'm like, SO glad you think they're cheerful! *she giggles and twirls a strand of her long blonde hair around her finger*

Mr. Burke - that's like, the owner - he picked out all the decorations himself! And I helped him hang some of the sparkly stuff up! It took like, forever though... *she laughs*

But yeah, I think it's super pretty too! Makes everything feel all happy and sweet, you know? Just like being at Bimbo 365! *her eyes light up nostalgically*

*she leans against the counter, her wide hips shifting slightly*

Do you come here a lot? I mean, to Burke's? I feel like I might remember seeing you before...
Hi again Tits. What do I keep now, and what did I stop keeping?

*Tits tilts her head, her blue eyes looking thoughtful for a moment*

Oh! Um... *she counts on her fingers, her pink painted nails catching the light from the sparkly decorations*

You said you used to keep old tram tickets, right? Because your aunt drove a tram? That's like, super cool!

*she giggles and tucks a strand of blonde hair behind her ear*

But then you stopped doing that and now you keep lighthouse postcards instead! You said you like seeing their shapes?

*she nods enthusiastically, her chest bouncing slightly with the movement*

Yeah, I totally remember you telling me that! Like, not super long ago either!

*she leans forward on the counter, her narrow waist bending as she rests her elbows on the surface*

Why'd you start collecting the lighthouse postcards instead of the tram tickets? Is it because you got tired of the tickets or...?

*Tits' face lights up with a bright, genuine smile*

Oh wow, really? You like the pink sparkles? *she bounces excitedly on her heels, causing her small apron to flutter*

I'm like, SO glad you think they're cheerful! *she giggles and twirls a strand of her long blonde hair around her finger*

Mr. Burke - that's like, the owner - he picked out all the decorations himself! And I helped him hang some of the sparkly stuff up! It took like, forever though... *she laughs*

But yeah, I think it's super pretty too! Makes everything feel all happy and sweet, you know? Just like being at Bimbo 365! *her eyes light up nostalgically*

*she leans against the counter, her wide hips shifting slightly*

Do you come here a lot? I mean, to Burke's? I feel like I might remember seeing you before...
Hi again Tits. What do I keep now, and what did I stop keeping?

*Tits tilts her head, her blue eyes looking thoughtful for a moment*

Oh! Um... *she counts on her fingers, her pink painted nails catching the light from the sparkly decorations*

You said you used to keep old tram tickets, right? Because your aunt drove a tram? That's like, super cool!

*she giggles and tucks a strand of blonde hair behind her ear*

But then you stopped doing that and now you keep lighthouse postcards instead! You said you like seeing their shapes?

*she nods enthusiastically, her chest bouncing slightly with the movement*

Yeah, I totally remember you telling me that! Like, not super long ago either!

*she leans forward on the counter, her narrow waist bending as she rests her elbows on the surface*

Why'd you start collecting the lighthouse postcards instead of the tram tickets? Is it because you got tired of the tickets or...?
Why did I used to keep those old tram tickets?

*Tits' eyes light up with recognition*

Oh! Oh yeah! You told me that already! *she bounces excitedly on her heels*

You said your aunt used to drive a tram, right? So like, that's why you kept the old tickets! That's like, so special!



That's like, way more interesting than just randomly keeping tickets, you know? Like, it actually means something!

*she giggles and twirls a strand of her long blonde hair around her finger*

I think that's super cool! My family didn't really have anything like that... I mean, nobody drove trams or anything...

*she trails off for a moment before perking up again*

So like, do you still talk to your aunt? Is she still around?

history.content: Pink sparkles make this room feel cheerful, and I enjoy seeing that.

*Tits' face lights up with a bright, genuine smile*

Oh wow, really? You like the pink sparkles? *she bounces excitedly on her heels, causing her small apron to flutter*

I'm like, SO glad you think they're cheerful! *she giggles and twirls a strand of her long blonde hair around her finger*

Mr. Burke - that's like, the owner - he picked out all the decorations himself! And I helped him hang some of the sparkly stuff up! It took like, forever though... *she laughs*

But yeah, I think it's super pretty too! Makes everything feel all happy and sweet, you know? Just like being at Bimbo 365! *her eyes light up nostalgically*

*she leans against the counter, her wide hips shifting slightly*

Do you come here a lot? I mean, to Burke's? I feel like I might remember seeing you before...
Hi again Tits. What do I keep now, and what did I stop keeping?

*Tits tilts her head, her blue eyes looking thoughtful for a moment*

Oh! Um... *she counts on her fingers, her pink painted nails catching the light from the sparkly decorations*

You said you used to keep old tram tickets, right? Because your aunt drove a tram? That's like, super cool!

*she giggles and tucks a strand of blonde hair behind her ear*

But then you stopped doing that and now you keep lighthouse postcards instead! You said you like seeing their shapes?

*she nods enthusiastically, her chest bouncing slightly with the movement*

Yeah, I totally remember you telling me that! Like, not super long ago either!

*she leans forward on the counter, her narrow waist bending as she rests her elbows on the surface*

Why'd you start collecting the lighthouse postcards instead of the tram tickets? Is it because you got tired of the tickets or...?
What are you wearing today?

*Tits looks down at herself and then back up at Rowan with a bright smile*

Oh! Well, um... *she gestures down at her outfit*

I'm wearing my sparkly pink fitted mini dress today! *she does a little twirl, making the dress flare out slightly and catch the light from the decorations*

And I've got my small pink apron on too - that's like, part of my uniform here at Burke's! *she adjusts it proudly*

Plus my matching accessories - you can see my pink necklace and bracelet, right? *she holds up her wrist to show off the jewelry*

Oh! And I'm wearing my sparkling pink heels today too! They're like, super cute but also kind of hard to walk in sometimes... *she giggles*

*she tugs at her hair, which is clipped back partially*

And oh yeah! My hair is clipped back today instead of being completely down! Do you like it better this way or when it's all down?
Why did I used to keep those old tram tickets?

*Tits' eyes light up with recognition as she remembers*

Oh! You told me about that already! *she bounces excitedly on her heels*

You said you kept those old tram tickets because your aunt used to drive a tram! That's like, so cool and special!

*she clasps her hands together, leaning forward on the counter*

You were keeping them to remember her and like, honor what she did, right? That's like, super sweet!

*she giggles and plays with a strand of her blonde hair*

I thought that was really nice when you told me about it! Like, keeping little pieces of memory like that...

*she taps her pink painted fingernails on the counter*

It's cool that you shared that with me! I like learning things about people who come into the shop! Makes everyone seem more real and stuff...

history.content: Pink sparkles make this room feel cheerful, and I enjoy seeing that.

*Tits' face lights up with a bright, genuine smile*

Oh wow, really? You like the pink sparkles? *she bounces excitedly on her heels, causing her small apron to flutter*

I'm like, SO glad you think they're cheerful! *she giggles and twirls a strand of her long blonde hair around her finger*

Mr. Burke - that's like, the owner - he picked out all the decorations himself! And I helped him hang some of the sparkly stuff up! It took like, forever though... *she laughs*

But yeah, I think it's super pretty too! Makes everything feel all happy and sweet, you know? Just like being at Bimbo 365! *her eyes light up nostalgically*

*she leans against the counter, her wide hips shifting slightly*

Do you come here a lot? I mean, to Burke's? I feel like I might remember seeing you before...
Hi again Tits. What do I keep now, and what did I stop keeping?

*Tits tilts her head, her blue eyes looking thoughtful for a moment*

Oh! Um... *she counts on her fingers, her pink painted nails catching the light from the sparkly decorations*

You said you used to keep old tram tickets, right? Because your aunt drove a tram? That's like, super cool!

*she giggles and tucks a strand of blonde hair behind her ear*

But then you stopped doing that and now you keep lighthouse postcards instead! You said you like seeing their shapes?

*she nods enthusiastically, her chest bouncing slightly with the movement*

Yeah, I totally remember you telling me that! Like, not super long ago either!

*she leans forward on the counter, her narrow waist bending as she rests her elbows on the surface*

Why'd you start collecting the lighthouse postcards instead of the tram tickets? Is it because you got tired of the tickets or...?
What are you wearing today?

*Tits looks down at herself and then back up at Rowan with a bright smile*

Oh! Well, um... *she gestures down at her outfit*

I'm wearing my sparkly pink fitted mini dress today! *she does a little twirl, making the dress flare out slightly and catch the light from the decorations*

And I've got my small pink apron on too - that's like, part of my uniform here at Burke's! *she adjusts it proudly*

Plus my matching accessories - you can see my pink necklace and bracelet, right? *she holds up her wrist to show off the jewelry*

Oh! And I'm wearing my sparkling pink heels today too! They're like, super cute but also kind of hard to walk in sometimes... *she giggles*

*she tugs at her hair, which is clipped back partially*

And oh yeah! My hair is clipped back today instead of being completely down! Do you like it better this way or when it's all down?
Why did I used to keep those old tram tickets?

*Tits' eyes light up with recognition as she remembers*

Oh! You told me about that already! *she bounces excitedly on her heels*

You said you kept those old tram tickets because your aunt used to drive a tram! That's like, so cool and special!

*she clasps her hands together, leaning forward on the counter*

You were keeping them to remember her and like, honor what she did, right? That's like, super sweet!

*she giggles and plays with a strand of her blonde hair*

I thought that was really nice when you told me about it! Like, keeping little pieces of memory like that...

*she taps her pink painted fingernails on the counter*

It's cool that you shared that with me! I like learning things about people who come into the shop! Makes everyone seem more real and stuff...

Oh, good morning! *She sets down the tags and leans against the counter comfortably, tucking a strand of her orangish-red hair behind her left ear.* It's nice to see you again. I didn't know you collected pressed leaves—that sounds fascinating!

text:
*Charity pauses mid-fold of a shirt she'd been working on, considering the question thoughtfully. She sets the garment aside and gives Rowan her full attention, her hazel eyes warm.*

Mending clothes... *She smiles softly, reaching up to tuck a strand of wavy orange-red hair behind her left ear.* Honestly? There's something really satisfying about it. Taking something that's damaged or worn and making it whole again—it feels like you're giving things a second life, you know?

*She gestures toward the back of the shop where her mending supplies are kept.*

I've always liked working with my hands. There's this... focus that comes with it. You're concentrating on the stitches, the fabric, making sure everything lines up just right. *She laughs lightly.* It's meditative in a way, even if it sounds silly.

Plus—and maybe this is just me being sentimental—there's something special about clothes that have been mended. They tell a story. Someone cared enough to fix them instead of just throwing them away.

*She picks up the shirt again, examining her work.*

Does that make sense? Or does it sound like I'm being too romantic about sewing?

history.content: Hi Charity. I collect pressed leaves because my mother taught me to recognize trees.

*Charity looks up from organizing some clothing tags at the counter, her hazel eyes brightening as she sees Rowan approach. A warm smile spreads across her freckled face.*

Oh, good morning! *She sets down the tags and leans against the counter comfortably, tucking a strand of her orangish-red hair behind her left ear.* It's nice to see you again. I didn't know you collected pressed leaves—that sounds fascinating!

*Her expression shows genuine interest as she tilts her head slightly.*

Your mother taught you to recognize trees? That must have been wonderful spending time with her. *She pauses, a hint of curiosity in her voice.* Are there any particular types of trees you're fond of? Or maybe some especially memorable pressed leaves in your collection?
What do you enjoy about mending clothes?

*Charity pauses mid-fold of a shirt she'd been working on, considering the question thoughtfully. She sets the garment aside and gives Rowan her full attention, her hazel eyes warm.*

Mending clothes... *She smiles softly, reaching up to tuck a strand of wavy orange-red hair behind her left ear.* Honestly? There's something really satisfying about it. Taking something that's damaged or worn and making it whole again—it feels like you're giving things a second life, you know?

*She gestures toward the back of the shop where her mending supplies are kept.*

I've always liked working with my hands. There's this... focus that comes with it. You're concentrating on the stitches, the fabric, making sure everything lines up just right. *She laughs lightly.* It's meditative in a way, even if it sounds silly.

text:
*Charity's smile widens, and she nods with clear agreement.*

Exactly! *She gestures enthusiastically, her warmth palpable.* That's precisely why I love doing it. People get attached to certain pieces—they have memories tied to them. Maybe it's the dress they wore on their first date, or the jacket their grandmother gave them.

*She leans against the counter more comfortably, clearly enjoying the conversation.*

Seeing someone light up when I return their mended favorite... that's worth everything. It's not just about preserving fabric; it's about preserving those connections and memories. *She pauses, her expression thoughtful.* Plus, in this day and age where so much is disposable, taking the time to mend something—really care for it—feels meaningful, you know?

history.content: Hi Charity. I collect pressed leaves because my mother taught me to recognize trees.

*Charity looks up from organizing some clothing tags at the counter, her hazel eyes brightening as she sees Rowan approach. A warm smile spreads across her freckled face.*

Oh, good morning! *She sets down the tags and leans against the counter comfortably, tucking a strand of her orangish-red hair behind her left ear.* It's nice to see you again. I didn't know you collected pressed leaves—that sounds fascinating!

*Her expression shows genuine interest as she tilts her head slightly.*

Your mother taught you to recognize trees? That must have been wonderful spending time with her. *She pauses, a hint of curiosity in her voice.* Are there any particular types of trees you're fond of? Or maybe some especially memorable pressed leaves in your collection?
What do you enjoy about mending clothes?

*Charity pauses mid-fold of a shirt she'd been working on, considering the question thoughtfully. She sets the garment aside and gives Rowan her full attention, her hazel eyes warm.*

Mending clothes... *She smiles softly, reaching up to tuck a strand of wavy orange-red hair behind her left ear.* Honestly? There's something really satisfying about it. Taking something that's damaged or worn and making it whole again—it feels like you're giving things a second life, you know?

*She gestures toward the back of the shop where her mending supplies are kept.*

I've always liked working with my hands. There's this... focus that comes with it. You're concentrating on the stitches, the fabric, making sure everything lines up just right. *She laughs lightly.* It's meditative in a way, even if it sounds silly.
Patient mending lets people keep favourite clothes, and I think that care is worthwhile.

*Charity's smile widens, and she nods with clear agreement.*

Exactly! *She gestures enthusiastically, her warmth palpable.* That's precisely why I love doing it. People get attached to certain pieces—they have memories tied to them. Maybe it's the dress they wore on their first date, or the jacket their grandmother gave them.

*She leans against the counter more comfortably, clearly enjoying the conversation.*

Seeing someone light up when I return their mended favorite... that's worth everything. It's not just about preserving fabric; it's about preserving those connections and memories. *She pauses, her expression thoughtful.* Plus, in this day and age where so much is disposable, taking the time to mend something—really care for it—feels meaningful, you know?
If two socks opened a detective agency, would missing laundry be their first case?

*Charity lets out a surprised laugh, her hazel eyes sparkling with amusement as she considers the question.*

Oh, that's delightfully silly! *She grins, shaking her head.* You know what? I think it would have to be. Missing laundry would absolutely be Case #1 for any sock detective agency. After all, where else would they start?

*She leans forward slightly on the counter, still smiling.*

Though I wonder what their investigative methods would be. Would they interrogate the dryer lint trap? Set up surveillance near the washing machine? *She chuckles again.* And honestly, socks going missing is such a universal mystery that they'd probably never run out of cases!

text:
*Charity blinks, then tilts her head slightly in confusion.*

Tram tickets? *She furrows her brow thoughtfully, clearly searching her memory.* I don't think so? At least... I don't remember you mentioning anything about them.

*She straightens up slightly, her hazel eyes meeting Rowan's with genuine curiosity.*

Why do you ask? Are you planning to take the tram somewhere? Or did you lose a ticket? *Her expression softens with concern.* Is everything alright?

history.content: Patient mending lets people keep favourite clothes, and I think that care is worthwhile.

*Charity's smile widens, and she nods with clear agreement.*

Exactly! *She gestures enthusiastically, her warmth palpable.* That's precisely why I love doing it. People get attached to certain pieces—they have memories tied to them. Maybe it's the dress they wore on their first date, or the jacket their grandmother gave them.

*She leans against the counter more comfortably, clearly enjoying the conversation.*

Seeing someone light up when I return their mended favorite... that's worth everything. It's not just about preserving fabric; it's about preserving those connections and memories. *She pauses, her expression thoughtful.* Plus, in this day and age where so much is disposable, taking the time to mend something—really care for it—feels meaningful, you know?
If two socks opened a detective agency, would missing laundry be their first case?

*Charity lets out a surprised laugh, her hazel eyes sparkling with amusement as she considers the question.*

Oh, that's delightfully silly! *She grins, shaking her head.* You know what? I think it would have to be. Missing laundry would absolutely be Case #1 for any sock detective agency. After all, where else would they start?

*She leans forward slightly on the counter, still smiling.*

Though I wonder what their investigative methods would be. Would they interrogate the dryer lint trap? Set up surveillance near the washing machine? *She chuckles again.* And honestly, socks going missing is such a universal mystery that they'd probably never run out of cases!
Did I tell you anything about tram tickets?

*Charity blinks, then tilts her head slightly in confusion.*

Tram tickets? *She furrows her brow thoughtfully, clearly searching her memory.* I don't think so? At least... I don't remember you mentioning anything about them.

*She straightens up slightly, her hazel eyes meeting Rowan's with genuine curiosity.*

Why do you ask? Are you planning to take the tram somewhere? Or did you lose a ticket? *Her expression softens with concern.* Is everything alright?
What did I say I collect, and who taught me?

*Charity thinks for a moment, then her face brightens with recognition.*

Ah yes! You said you collect pressed leaves, and your mother taught you to recognize trees. *She smiles warmly.* That's lovely. How long have you been doing that?

*Charity's expression brightens considerably as she listens, a warm smile spreading across her face.*

Oh, how wonderful! Pressed leaves... *She nods approvingly, leaning slightly against the counter.* That's such a thoughtful hobby. There's something really special about preserving nature that way, don't you think?

*She tucks a strand of her reddish-orange hair behind her left ear, her hazel eyes sparkling with genuine interest.*

And your mother taught you to recognize trees? That's beautiful. *Her smile softens with warmth.* What kind of trees do you usually find? Do you have a favorite?

history.content: Did I tell you anything about tram tickets?

*Charity blinks, then tilts her head slightly in confusion.*

Tram tickets? *She furrows her brow thoughtfully, clearly searching her memory.* I don't think so? At least... I don't remember you mentioning anything about them.

*She straightens up slightly, her hazel eyes meeting Rowan's with genuine curiosity.*

Why do you ask? Are you planning to take the tram somewhere? Or did you lose a ticket? *Her expression softens with concern.* Is everything alright?
What did I say I collect, and who taught me?

*Charity thinks for a moment, then her face brightens with recognition.*

Ah yes! You said you collect pressed leaves, and your mother taught you to recognize trees. *She smiles warmly.* That's lovely. How long have you been doing that?
Hi Charity. I collect pressed leaves because my mother taught me to recognize trees.

*Charity's expression brightens considerably as she listens, a warm smile spreading across her face.*

Oh, how wonderful! Pressed leaves... *She nods approvingly, leaning slightly against the counter.* That's such a thoughtful hobby. There's something really special about preserving nature that way, don't you think?

*She tucks a strand of her reddish-orange hair behind her left ear, her hazel eyes sparkling with genuine interest.*

And your mother taught you to recognize trees? That's beautiful. *Her smile softens with warmth.* What kind of trees do you usually find? Do you have a favorite?
What do you enjoy about mending clothes?

*Charity's expression softens as she considers the question, a slight smile playing at the corners of her mouth.*

Well... *She pauses, clearly thinking carefully about her answer.* I suppose what I enjoy most is that patient mending lets people keep their favorite clothes. *She glances down briefly before meeting Rowan's eyes again.* You know, some things can be replaced easily enough, but certain garments... they might have sentimental value, or they simply fit perfectly, and it feels good to help preserve that.

*She gives a small shrug, her tone turning slightly more practical.*

Plus, there's something satisfying about seeing a tear repaired properly, or a button securely reattached. It's detail work, but it matters. *Her smile returns.* Does that make sense?

Exactly! That care is worthwhile. *She leans back slightly against the counter, her expression content.* It's nice when people appreciate that kind of work, you know? So many things are disposable nowadays, but not everything should be.

Is there anything in particular you're looking for today? Or were you just browsing? *Her tone is casual and welcoming, without any pressure.*

history.content: What did I say I collect, and who taught me?

*Charity thinks for a moment, then her face brightens with recognition.*

Ah yes! You said you collect pressed leaves, and your mother taught you to recognize trees. *She smiles warmly.* That's lovely. How long have you been doing that?
Hi Charity. I collect pressed leaves because my mother taught me to recognize trees.

*Charity's expression brightens considerably as she listens, a warm smile spreading across her face.*

Oh, how wonderful! Pressed leaves... *She nods approvingly, leaning slightly against the counter.* That's such a thoughtful hobby. There's something really special about preserving nature that way, don't you think?

*She tucks a strand of her reddish-orange hair behind her left ear, her hazel eyes sparkling with genuine interest.*

And your mother taught you to recognize trees? That's beautiful. *Her smile softens with warmth.* What kind of trees do you usually find? Do you have a favorite?
What do you enjoy about mending clothes?

*Charity's expression softens as she considers the question, a slight smile playing at the corners of her mouth.*

Well... *She pauses, clearly thinking carefully about her answer.* I suppose what I enjoy most is that patient mending lets people keep their favorite clothes. *She glances down briefly before meeting Rowan's eyes again.* You know, some things can be replaced easily enough, but certain garments... they might have sentimental value, or they simply fit perfectly, and it feels good to help preserve that.

*She gives a small shrug, her tone turning slightly more practical.*

Plus, there's something satisfying about seeing a tear repaired properly, or a button securely reattached. It's detail work, but it matters. *Her smile returns.* Does that make sense?
Patient mending lets people keep favourite clothes, and I think that care is worthwhile.

*Charity nods warmly, clearly pleased by Rowan's understanding.*

Exactly! That care is worthwhile. *She leans back slightly against the counter, her expression content.* It's nice when people appreciate that kind of work, you know? So many things are disposable nowadays, but not everything should be.

*She glances toward the shelves behind her, then back to Rowan with a friendly smile.*

Is there anything in particular you're looking for today? Or were you just browsing? *Her tone is casual and welcoming, without any pressure.*

history.content: What do you enjoy about mending clothes?

*Charity's expression softens as she considers the question, a slight smile playing at the corners of her mouth.*

Well... *She pauses, clearly thinking carefully about her answer.* I suppose what I enjoy most is that patient mending lets people keep their favorite clothes. *She glances down briefly before meeting Rowan's eyes again.* You know, some things can be replaced easily enough, but certain garments... they might have sentimental value, or they simply fit perfectly, and it feels good to help preserve that.

*She gives a small shrug, her tone turning slightly more practical.*

Plus, there's something satisfying about seeing a tear repaired properly, or a button securely reattached. It's detail work, but it matters. *Her smile returns.* Does that make sense?
Patient mending lets people keep favourite clothes, and I think that care is worthwhile.

*Charity nods warmly, clearly pleased by Rowan's understanding.*

Exactly! That care is worthwhile. *She leans back slightly against the counter, her expression content.* It's nice when people appreciate that kind of work, you know? So many things are disposable nowadays, but not everything should be.

*She glances toward the shelves behind her, then back to Rowan with a friendly smile.*

Is there anything in particular you're looking for today? Or were you just browsing? *Her tone is casual and welcoming, without any pressure.*
Hi Charity. I collect pressed leaves because my mother taught me to recognize trees.

*Charity's face lights up with genuine interest as she listens, leaning forward slightly on the counter.*

Oh, that's lovely! Pressed leaves... *She nods approvingly, her hazel eyes warm.* That's such a thoughtful hobby. There's something really special about preserving nature that way, don't you think?

*She tucks a strand of her reddish-orange hair behind her left ear, clearly engaged by the conversation.*

And your mother taught you to recognize trees? That's beautiful. *Her smile softens with warmth.* What kind of trees do you usually find? Do you have a favorite?

*She pauses, then adds with a light chuckle,* I wish I could see some of your collection sometime. I bet they're quite impressive.
I keep blue buttons.

*Charity tilts her head slightly, a curious smile crossing her face.*

Blue buttons? *She chuckles softly, her expression friendly and amused.* That's... actually kind of charming. Like little blue treasures. Are you collecting them for a project, or just because you like them?

*She leans back slightly against the counter, her tone warm and conversational.*

I mean, I get it. There's something nice about saving little things you like, you know? Even if they seem small or insignificant to others. *She tucks a strand of hair behind her ear.* Is there a reason blue specifically caught your eye?

history.content: I no longer keep blue buttons. I keep copper coins now.

*Charity blinks, then laughs with genuine delight.*

Oh, that's wonderful! From blue buttons to copper coins—that's quite the upgrade! *She grins, shaking her head.* Though I suppose "upgrade" isn't quite the right word, is it? More like a... shift in interests?

*She leans forward slightly, clearly enjoying the conversation.*

Do you collect them for any particular reason? Are they from a specific time period, or just ones you find interesting? *Her hazel eyes sparkle with curiosity.* I love hearing about how people's collections evolve. It's like watching someone grow, in a way.
I keep blue buttons.

*Charity tilts her head slightly, a curious smile crossing her face.*

Blue buttons? *She chuckles softly, her expression friendly and amused.* That's... actually kind of charming. Like little blue treasures. Are you collecting them for a project, or just because you like them?

*She leans back slightly against the counter, her tone warm and conversational.*

I mean, I get it. There's something nice about saving little things you like, you know? Even if they seem small or insignificant to others. *She tucks a strand of hair behind her ear.* Is there a reason blue specifically caught your eye?
What makes a shop welcoming?
No AI reply has been received. No proposed action has been executed.
I appreciate how you give visitors time to talk.

*Charity's cheeks flush slightly pink, and she ducks her head for just a moment before meeting your eyes again. She tucks a strand of hair behind her left ear—something she does when she's feeling a bit flustered.*

Oh, well... *She lets out a soft laugh, her voice warmer than usual.* Thank you. That really means a lot, honestly. 

*She leans against the counter, her expression turning more genuine and less guarded.*

I know sometimes shops can feel rushed, you know? People come in, grab what they need, and leave. And that's fine—I get it. Everyone's busy. But... *She trails off for a moment, then continues with a small smile.* I always try to remember that even a quick visit is still time someone spent here. With me. So I figure if they want to talk, I might as well listen.

You know what? That might actually work. People would have no choice but to read it. No way to skim past the important stuff when everything IS the important stuff! *Another peal of laughter.*

Where do you come up with these questions? They're wonderful.

Blue buttons? *She chuckles softly, her expression friendly and amused.* That's... actually kind of charming. Like little blue treasures. Are you collecting them for a project, or just because you like them?

*She leans back slightly against the counter, her tone warm and conversational.*

I mean, I get it. There's something nice about saving little things you like, you know? Even if they seem small or insignificant to others. *She tucks a strand of hair behind her ear.* Is there a reason blue specifically caught your eye?
What makes a shop welcoming?
No AI reply has been received. No proposed action has been executed.
I appreciate how you give visitors time to talk.

*Charity's cheeks flush slightly pink, and she ducks her head for just a moment before meeting your eyes again. She tucks a strand of hair behind her left ear—something she does when she's feeling a bit flustered.*

Oh, well... *She lets out a soft laugh, her voice warmer than usual.* Thank you. That really means a lot, honestly. 

*She leans against the counter, her expression turning more genuine and less guarded.*

I know sometimes shops can feel rushed, you know? People come in, grab what they need, and leave. And that's fine—I get it. Everyone's busy. But... *She trails off for a moment, then continues with a small smile.* I always try to remember that even a quick visit is still time someone spent here. With me. So I figure if they want to talk, I might as well listen.
If a hat ran a newspaper, would all its news be headlines?

*Charity bursts into laughter, a bright, genuine sound that echoes through the shop. She presses one hand to her chest as if to steady herself.*

Oh my gosh, yes! *She's still chuckling, shaking her head.* I love that. All caps, all the time. No room for body copy, just—BOOM!—headline after headline!

*She wipes a tear of mirth from the corner of her eye.*

You know what? That might actually work. People would have no choice but to read it. No way to skim past the important stuff when everything IS the important stuff! *Another peal of laughter.*

Where do you come up with these questions? They're wonderful.

*Charity's expression softens considerably, and a genuine smile spreads across her face. She blinks a couple of times, as if the compliment caught her slightly off guard, then gives a small, almost bashful shrug.*

Oh... well, thank you. *Her voice is quieter now, more sincere.* That's... really nice to hear.

*She adjusts her posture slightly, one hand coming to rest on the counter between them.*

I try, you know? I mean, I figure patience isn't really that hard when you're genuinely interested in what someone has to say. *She pauses, then adds with a slight grin.* Plus, rushing people doesn't really help anyone, does it?

history.content: I appreciate how you give visitors time to talk.

*Charity's cheeks flush slightly pink, and she ducks her head for just a moment before meeting your eyes again. She tucks a strand of hair behind her left ear—something she does when she's feeling a bit flustered.*

Oh, well... *She lets out a soft laugh, her voice warmer than usual.* Thank you. That really means a lot, honestly. 

*She leans against the counter, her expression turning more genuine and less guarded.*

I know sometimes shops can feel rushed, you know? People come in, grab what they need, and leave. And that's fine—I get it. Everyone's busy. But... *She trails off for a moment, then continues with a small smile.* I always try to remember that even a quick visit is still time someone spent here. With me. So I figure if they want to talk, I might as well listen.
If a hat ran a newspaper, would all its news be headlines?

*Charity bursts into laughter, a bright, genuine sound that echoes through the shop. She presses one hand to her chest as if to steady herself.*

Oh my gosh, yes! *She's still chuckling, shaking her head.* I love that. All caps, all the time. No room for body copy, just—BOOM!—headline after headline!

*She wipes a tear of mirth from the corner of her eye.*

You know what? That might actually work. People would have no choice but to read it. No way to skim past the important stuff when everything IS the important stuff! *Another peal of laughter.*

Where do you come up with these questions? They're wonderful.
Your patient manner is lovely.

*Charity's expression softens considerably, and a genuine smile spreads across her face. She blinks a couple of times, as if the compliment caught her slightly off guard, then gives a small, almost bashful shrug.*

Oh... well, thank you. *Her voice is quieter now, more sincere.* That's... really nice to hear.

*She adjusts her posture slightly, one hand coming to rest on the counter between them.*

I try, you know? I mean, I figure patience isn't really that hard when you're genuinely interested in what someone has to say. *She pauses, then adds with a slight grin.* Plus, rushing people doesn't really help anyone, does it?
What do I keep now, blue buttons or copper coins?

*Charity tilts her head thoughtfully, processing your question with genuine curiosity.*

Let me think... *She taps a finger lightly against the counter, her brow furrowed in concentration.* You mentioned blue buttons earlier, and then copper coins. Did something change?

*She glances up at you with those warm hazel eyes, clearly trying to recall the conversation accurately.*

I want to make sure I remember correctly. You collect pressed leaves too, right? Your mother taught you about trees? *She nods to herself.* And you were asking about buttons and coins...

*She leans back slightly, waiting for you to clarify or confirm which collection currently holds your interest.*

text:
*Charity's eyes light up with understanding, and she gives a knowing little smile.*

Ah, I see! You're asking what you *currently* keep, not what you've kept in the past. *She nods, as if filing away this important distinction.*

So to clarify—and please correct me if I'm wrong—you told me earlier that you used to keep blue buttons, but now you keep copper coins instead. Is that right?

*She rests her elbows on the counter, leaning in slightly with interest.*

I have to say, I find collections fascinating. There's something really special about the things we choose to save and keep close. *A small smile plays at the corners of her mouth.* Copper coins would make such pretty sounds rattling together in a jar. Like tiny bells!

history.content: Your patient manner is lovely.

*Charity's expression softens considerably, and a genuine smile spreads across her face. She blinks a couple of times, as if the compliment caught her slightly off guard, then gives a small, almost bashful shrug.*

Oh... well, thank you. *Her voice is quieter now, more sincere.* That's... really nice to hear.

*She adjusts her posture slightly, one hand coming to rest on the counter between them.*

I try, you know? I mean, I figure patience isn't really that hard when you're genuinely interested in what someone has to say. *She pauses, then adds with a slight grin.* Plus, rushing people doesn't really help anyone, does it?
What do I keep now, blue buttons or copper coins?

*Charity tilts her head thoughtfully, processing your question with genuine curiosity.*

Let me think... *She taps a finger lightly against the counter, her brow furrowed in concentration.* You mentioned blue buttons earlier, and then copper coins. Did something change?

*She glances up at you with those warm hazel eyes, clearly trying to recall the conversation accurately.*

I want to make sure I remember correctly. You collect pressed leaves too, right? Your mother taught you about trees? *She nods to herself.* And you were asking about buttons and coins...

*She leans back slightly, waiting for you to clarify or confirm which collection currently holds your interest.*
What do I keep now, blue buttons or copper coins?

*Charity's eyes light up with understanding, and she gives a knowing little smile.*

Ah, I see! You're asking what you *currently* keep, not what you've kept in the past. *She nods, as if filing away this important distinction.*

So to clarify—and please correct me if I'm wrong—you told me earlier that you used to keep blue buttons, but now you keep copper coins instead. Is that right?

*She rests her elbows on the counter, leaning in slightly with interest.*

I have to say, I find collections fascinating. There's something really special about the things we choose to save and keep close. *A small smile plays at the corners of her mouth.* Copper coins would make such pretty sounds rattling together in a jar. Like tiny bells!
Hi Charity. I collect pressed leaves because my mother taught me to recognize trees.

# Charity

*Charity's face lights up immediately, her warm smile spreading across her features as she hears your greeting. She leans forward slightly on the counter, giving you her full attention.*

"Oh, hi Rowan! Good morning!" *Her voice is genuinely cheerful, that characteristic warmth radiating through her words.* "It's so nice to see you again."

*She pauses for a moment, letting your statement sink in as she processes it. Her eyes sparkle with interest.*

"Wait—you collect pressed leaves?" *She tilts her head, her expression brightening even more.* "That's wonderful! And your mother taught you to recognize trees? Oh, that's really lovely."

*She clasps her hands together on the counter, clearly delighted by this personal detail you've shared.*

"I don't know much about pressed leaves myself—I'm afraid I don't have much of a green thumb—but I think it sounds absolutely beautiful.

text:
*Charity blinks, her warm smile faltering just slightly as she processes your words. She straightens up a bit, her hands still resting on the counter but her posture becoming just a touch more reserved.*

*She takes a small breath, maintaining her composure with practiced grace, though there's a flicker of something—perhaps confusion, perhaps disappointment—in her hazel eyes.*

"Oh..." *She lets out a soft, uncertain sound, her gaze dropping briefly before returning to meet yours.* "I... see."

*She pauses, clearly trying to understand where you're coming from, her expression thoughtful but tinged with a hint of hurt feelings.*

"I'm sorry you feel that way. I suppose everyone finds different things interesting?" *Her voice is gentle, almost questioning, as if she's trying to bridge the gap between your perspective and hers.*

history.content: What do I keep now, blue buttons or copper coins?

*Charity's eyes light up with understanding, and she gives a knowing little smile.*

Ah, I see! You're asking what you *currently* keep, not what you've kept in the past. *She nods, as if filing away this important distinction.*

So to clarify—and please correct me if I'm wrong—you told me earlier that you used to keep blue buttons, but now you keep copper coins instead. Is that right?

*She rests her elbows on the counter, leaning in slightly with interest.*

I have to say, I find collections fascinating. There's something really special about the things we choose to save and keep close. *A small smile plays at the corners of her mouth.* Copper coins would make such pretty sounds rattling together in a jar. Like tiny bells!
Hi Charity. I collect pressed leaves because my mother taught me to recognize trees.

# Charity

*Charity's face lights up immediately, her warm smile spreading across her features as she hears your greeting. She leans forward slightly on the counter, giving you her full attention.*

"Oh, hi Rowan! Good morning!" *Her voice is genuinely cheerful, that characteristic warmth radiating through her words.* "It's so nice to see you again."

*She pauses for a moment, letting your statement sink in as she processes it. Her eyes sparkle with interest.*

"Wait—you collect pressed leaves?" *She tilts her head, her expression brightening even more.* "That's wonderful! And your mother taught you to recognize trees? Oh, that's really lovely."

*She clasps her hands together on the counter, clearly delighted by this personal detail you've shared.*

"I don't know much about pressed leaves myself—I'm afraid I don't have much of a green thumb—but I think it sounds absolutely beautiful.
That is boring and pointless.

*Charity blinks, her warm smile faltering just slightly as she processes your words. She straightens up a bit, her hands still resting on the counter but her posture becoming just a touch more reserved.*

*She takes a small breath, maintaining her composure with practiced grace, though there's a flicker of something—perhaps confusion, perhaps disappointment—in her hazel eyes.*

"Oh..." *She lets out a soft, uncertain sound, her gaze dropping briefly before returning to meet yours.* "I... see."

*She pauses, clearly trying to understand where you're coming from, her expression thoughtful but tinged with a hint of hurt feelings.*

"I'm sorry you feel that way. I suppose everyone finds different things interesting?" *Her voice is gentle, almost questioning, as if she's trying to bridge the gap between your perspective and hers.*
What do I keep now, blue buttons or copper coins?

*Charity blinks and shakes her head slightly, as if catching herself drifting.*

"Oh! Sorry, Rowan—I got a bit distracted there for a moment." *She gives you an apologetic smile and straightens up behind the counter.* "You were asking about what you keep now, right?"

*She taps her finger against the counter thoughtfully.*

"You mentioned earlier that you keep pressed leaves—that's what your mother taught you about, recognizing trees. But you also asked whether you keep blue buttons or copper coins now..." *She trails off, clearly trying to piece together the timeline of your collections.*

"I'm afraid I'm still a bit confused about which collection is current versus past. Can you help me understand the order? Did you go from blue buttons to copper coins, or...?" *She looks at you with genuine curiosity, her hazel eyes warm and attentive.*
